paragraphs.source_en:
to them — we, clogged by “error, ignorance, and strife”, see them not, till we are fitted by purification
and improvement for their higher state. For myself, no religious doctrine, nor philosophical precept,
can shake the faith that a mind so original, so delicately and beautifully moulded, as Shelley’s, so
endowed with wondrous powers and eagle-eyed genius — so good, so pure, would never be shattered
and dispersed by the Creator; but that the qualities and consciousness that formed him, are not only
indestructible in themselves, but in the form under which they were united here, and that to become
worthy of him is to assure the bliss of a reunion’ (i pp. xv–xvi).
